persons.name: Gvastikadhani
persons.evidence: kathavagvastikadhani karmmā cājye yo kekāyāva devyandrakarmmā cājyena

relations.evidence: karmmā cājye yo kekāyāva devyandrakarmmā cājyena

purpose: possibly offered to the goddess Sarasvatī (thva sarasvati deva yā ...); uncertain
notes: The cataloguer could not understand the Newari clause after the stanza: 'thva sarasvati deva yā śiro kathavagvastikadhani karmmā cājye yo kekāyāva devyandrakarmmā cājyena thava āṣalasena vavamacātośene yātāhleyājulo śubha'. A tentative reading: 'This [book] belongs to the goddess Sarasvatī; Devendra Karmācārya, son (kāya) of ...dhani Karmācārya, wrote it in his own letters (thava ākhalasena) and offered it (?)'. 'devyandra' = Devendra; 'karmmā cājye/cājyena' = Karmācārya with the instrumental case. 'yo kekāyāva' may be a corruption of 'yā kāya va' (son of), but that is uncertain. The son_of relation p1→p2 is therefore low certainty. The father's name (?) is corrupt: 'śiro kathavagvastikadhani' could hide a name ending in -dhana/-dhani, perhaps with an honorific such as śiromaṇi. Sarasvatī is a deity and is not listed as a person. The colophon has no date and no place.
